fixes.explanation: That's the heart of this whole psalm, friend: "He heals the brokenhearted and binds up their wounds." Healing is what the verse says He does. I think a verse that tender is worth reading twice. Go back and read it once more, nice and slow.
That sounds like a nice picture, but the psalm doesn't say it. What it says is, "He calls them each by name." Every star gets a name.

Nice try, but this psalm doesn't say that about the stars. It says, "He determines the number of the stars; He calls them each by name." My mustache gets tired just packing one cookie box, so moving stars by hand sounds like a lot. The detail the psalm gives is the names.

True. The psalm says, "Great is our Lord, and mighty in power; His understanding has no limit." No limit at all, not even a little one at the edge. I can't even keep track of my own mixing bowls, so this one is hard for me to picture.
The psalm actually says, "His understanding has no limit." So it's true, not false. Not a single limit anywhere. The same verse says, "Great is our Lord, and mighty in power…"

Mighty sounds like it could fit, but the psalm doesn't say it. It says, "The LORD sustains the humble, but casts the wicked to the ground." The verse puts the humble on one side and the wicked on the other. The humble are the ones He sustains, and mighty isn't on either side.

Clever is a fine thing to be. But the verse doesn't say it. It says, "The LORD sustains the humble, but casts the wicked to the ground." The contrast in this verse is the humble on one side and the wicked on the other. Cleverness never comes up.

That's it: "Sing to the LORD with thanksgiving…" This is a song with a thank-you inside it. I've got a LOT to be thankful for, like a gold base, a warm oven and the angel who called me out of a junk drawer. So this one comes easy to me.

Yep. God "…makes grass to grow on the hills." The same verse says He covers the sky with clouds and prepares rain for the earth. Three things God does, and grass is the one in the blank. Hills, I love that.

Thorns would be a prickly surprise, but that's not in this verse. The psalm says God "…makes grass to grow on the hills." Grass is the word for that blank. The same verse also says He covers the sky with clouds and prepares rain for the earth.

False is right. The psalm says, "He does not delight in the strength of the horse; He takes no pleasure in the legs of a man." Both the horse's strength and a man's legs are things He doesn't delight in. I think that takes a little pressure off, because I will never win a race.

I love learning, and I would happily show off my recipe collection. But this verse doesn't measure who knows the most. It says, "The LORD is pleased with those who fear Him, who hope in His loving devotion." Fearing Him and hoping in Him are what the psalm names, so that's the answer.

True. The psalm says, "His word runs swiftly." God sends forth His command to the earth, and it goes out at speed. Nobody has to chase it down. You know when you text someone and wait all afternoon for an answer? This is the opposite, and it impresses me.

That's it: "He declares His word to Jacob, His statutes and judgments to Israel." Jacob and Israel are both names the psalm uses here. God also gave Jacob the name Israel (Genesis 32:28). God declared His word to them.

Those are real nations in the Bible, but they're not named in this verse. The psalm says, "He declares His word to Jacob, His statutes and judgments to Israel." The answer is Jacob and Israel. The psalm's last verse adds, "He has done this for no other nation…"
Edom and Moab are good guesses, but this verse doesn't name them. The psalm says, "He declares His word to Jacob, His statutes and judgments to Israel." The answer is Jacob and Israel.
